entries.value:
A few things that might not show up elsewhere in this form. Most of my strongest work has been in systems where the cost of a wrong action is real, not just an incorrect output. In a Playwright-based job-application agent I built in TypeScript, I used SQLite as the single source of truth and put every mutating capability behind fail-closed environment flags, because browser automation gets dangerous the moment application state can diverge across processes. I also built a validation ladder so a capability is not called working until it has been confirmed against the level of reality it claims to support. That instinct maps closely to trading and risk software, where correctness and observability matter more than clever abstractions.

On the modeling side, I build the ML core of an anomaly-detection and alert-prioritization system: event ingestion, temporal sequence models over event streams, anomaly scoring, and a learning-to-rank layer, served through a versioned FastAPI microservice. Alert prioritization is a real concern there, since a detector that fires constantly just creates a second problem.

I would be happy on either a low-level systems or applied-ML team, and I care most about owning a meaningful piece end to end.

entries.value:
1. Python. Most of my modeling and data work is in Python: temporal sequence models and anomaly scoring over event streams at SAC Nexus, served through a versioned FastAPI microservice; XGBoost with SHAP-based feature selection and G-formula causal simulations on a roughly 10 million record survey dataset; a PyTorch CNN for facial-landmark prediction; and an SIR-style epidemiological model built from its differential equations.

2. TypeScript. I use it when the system needs strict state and safety guarantees rather than numerical work. I built a Playwright-based job-application agent in TypeScript and Node where every application moves through an explicit state machine, Zod validates inputs, and SQLite is the single source of truth, and I built tSearch, a talent-discovery pipeline, on the same stack.

I have also written C/C++ for a microcontroller-based dust sensor and Swift/SwiftUI for an iOS health app shipped into a Hopkins pilot, so I am comfortable picking up whatever language a team already works in.
